note:
v1, WHOLE (first round, composed from scratch): PHASE MARGIN, the first storm. 98 -> 108 bpm (flat across both 16-bar seams), D with the Neapolitan Eb, 128 bars, 299 s.
- E3 "the undertow" (posted in motifs.md): a 7-beat bass riff (E2 x4) on D | Eb | C, with its storm harmony Dm(add9) | Ebmaj7#11 | C11 (D4 common to all).
- THE STORM AS ARITHMETIC: E1 (20 sixteenths), E2 (7) and E3 (28) run against the bar, each PHASED so that all four land on bar 88's downbeat. Before it they collide: E1 displaced/inverted/fragmented on an NES pulse, E2 on chip-metal, E3 on a PM bass with dropped notes and octave throws, a 909 broken by Euclidean rotations plus NES noise rolls; stutter and crush lanes deepen through the eyewall; tracker arps (stepped LFO, 1/32) walk each chord's intervals. An EYE (bars 62-66: dust + sub only) and a BREAK (86-88: riser, the whispered line whole).
- THE LOCK (bar 88): E3 re-barred 2+2+4, E2 seven sixteenths and a rest, E1 without its rest - one groove; held shard chords, E1 an octave up; a pvoc robot sings "nothing here is late" on E1's notes (track.e1.key).
- Seams: the infall lenses t2's E2/E1 (chip shards, a cloud-shredded dust pad, no sub); the outfall redshifts (-7 st) the riff, E1 and shards, closes the master two octaves, and holds Dm(add9) at pitch with D4 under it for t4 to lift (agreed rows in mixplan.md).
- Scores: s0 84.571 / s11 84.639. Flow 70.6 (out-join to t4 5.4 dB / 3.23; in from t2 9.7 / 8.48). Recurrence 23 is the next job: share 0.92 is ABOVE the 0.25-0.7 band - the sections are too alike, so the next rounds give storm, eye, lock and crest distinct textures. Spectrum 91.8 (44 Hz short). Whisper/robot not yet intelligible (ASR).
-11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29.
next: contrast between sections (recurrence share 0.92 > 0.7): give the front, eyewall, crest distinct textures; voice clarity at the lock; 44 Hz

note:
v3, PALETTE. T3_R3=ring (=none reproduces v2). Two swaps, both away from album staples:
- E1's LEAD: nes-pulse-lead (a staple: 5 of 8 songs) -> a3-ring, a saw RING-MODULATED by a sine at 1.414:1 (the engine's layer ringmod, which no preset uses) over a quiet square an octave down. Its ring mix rides an auto lane: 0.85 through the storm (inharmonic, metallic, abrasive) and 0.1 from the lock, so the storm resolves in the timbre as well as the rhythm. Both E1 tracks (e1, e1hi) swapped.
- THE STORM'S SNARE: the 909 (3 songs) -> ks-drum (Karplus-Strong skin, unused on the album), TUNED to the key - accents on D4, ghosts on A4 - through the storm's stutter/crush lanes; at bar 88 the 909 snare takes over, so the lock arrives as a change of drum as well.
- Measured on full renders against v2 on today's pin and mix-window flow: v2 now 84.025 -> v3 84.705 (s0) / 84.981 (s11); variety 89.9 -> 92.9/94.4, spectrum 91.6 -> 92.0. Sections --against v2: every window changed (-13 dB in the infall, ~-23 dB elsewhere). -11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29.
- New flow (mix windows) shows the out-seam's problem: my crest body before the t4 crossfade has ~+32 dB at 10-15 kHz against t4's warm body (hats, ride, glass) - next.

note:
v4, SECTION (w7, bars 72-84, 2:52-3:19 - the lock assembling, flagged static). T3_R4=align (=none reproduces v3). THE ARITHMETIC MADE AUDIBLE:
- A COUNT: glass ticks on every downbeat climb D Phrygian two bars a step - D5 Eb5 F5 G5 A5 Bb5 C6 - and stop at the break, so bar 88 (the lock) is the D they were climbing to.
- ALIGNMENT HITS: wherever a cycle already lines up with the bar before the lock - E1 (20 sixteenths) at bars 73, 78, 83; E2 (7) and E3 (28) together at 74 and 81 - a crash, a kick and a shard chord (Dm(add9) up an octave) land on that downbeat; the double alignments come after an eighth of held breath (every drum cut). The listener hears the cycles catching up, flash by flash, before they all coincide at 88.
- THE VOICE CLEARS: the bar-82 fragment ("nothing here is") moves from the pvoc whisper to a dry spoken voice - the first clear words in the song, as the arithmetic clears (ASR: "Nothing he missed", where the whisper read nothing).
- Local: sections --against v3 change only w7 (-15.1 dB) and w8 (-17.8, the tails into the break). s0 84.731 / s11 85.276 (v3 84.705 / 84.981). -11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29.
next: out-seam to t4: darken the crest's last bars before the crossfade (10-15 kHz +32 dB vs t4 on the mix windows); storm-section contrast (recurrence share 0.92)

v6, WHOLE-TRACK RE-HARMONISATION (drawn: section; overridden by Harry's 00:30 direction - "atonal ... missing hook ... big changes wanted"). T3_R6=tonal (=none reproduces v5). TONE IS HOME; the storm stays hard in TIME (20/7/28 cycles, broken kit, stutter) but not in pitch:
- E3 v2: the undertow on D | Bb | C (i - VI - VII), harmony Dm(add9) | Bbmaj7 | C(add9) - no Neapolitan ground; the shards, dust, floor, crab-canon glass and outfall all follow it.
- THE LOCK RESOLVES HOME every two bars: Dm | Bb | C | Dm (2+2+2+2), the riff's held last beat C -> D (it had read C major: the old 2+2+4 held C for half the cycle).
- The tracker arps walk consonant intervals (m(add9), maj7, add9); the ring lead's modulator at 2:1 - harmonic sidebands, in tune - instead of 1.414; the alignment count climbs D Aeolian (E, not Eb).
- THE HOOK: E1 stated plainly, upright and doubled an octave up, for two full cycles at the top of the front (bar 17), the eyewall (41) and after the eye (67), so the storm's fragments and inversions are heard against the tune.
- Key clarity (chroma vs Krumhansl): storm D minor r 0.70 -> 0.68 (still D minor), lock+crest D minor r 0.65 -> 0.82.
- s0 93.412 / s11 93.296 (rebaselined v5 92.264 / 92.915); spectrum 93.9, flow 68.3. -11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29.
